name: The relationship between domestic violence and shooting incidents in New York City
description:
This dataset contains public safety data for New York City police precincts, linking counts of shooting incidents with counts of domestic violence incidents. Each row represents a precinct (with a few borough- and city-level summary rows), and includes total shootings, total domestic violence incidents, population, and calculated rates per population for both measures. The data also includes breakdowns of actual versus expected shooting and domestic violence counts by race and by sex, along with corresponding New York City population figures used to derive those expectations.

With 83 rows and 43 columns, the dataset supports analyses of whether precincts with higher domestic violence rates also experience more shootings, comparisons of observed incident counts against demographically expected counts to examine disparities, and geographic comparisons across precincts. It could be used by researchers, policymakers, or analysts studying the overlap between domestic violence and gun violence, allocating public safety resources, or investigating demographic patterns in violent incidents. Note that many of the race- and sex-breakdown columns are populated in only one row
